subject: Hosted API pricing: split of system/tool tokens and rounding policy
body:
From: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@datafirst.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@datafirst.ai>, DataFirst.ai Procurement <procurement@datafirst.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing: split of system/tool tokens and rounding policy

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — DataFirst is evaluating Redwood for our conversational search layer. Procurement has a couple of detailed questions from engineering/finance about how tokens show up on the invoice so we can model costs accurately:

- When you say "input" vs "output" tokens, where do system prompts (the persistent system message) get counted? Are they folded into input or listed separately?
- Tool calls: if an API call triggers an external tool (e.g., a reranker or a scraped content tool) that returns text, is that tool output charged as output tokens on the same line, or is it a separate line item?
- Rounding: do you round token counts per request (ceiling) or only at invoice aggregation? If you round per-request, do you round to whole tokens, tens, or some other bucket?

Can you send a short write-up we can share with finance + a sample invoice calculation for a 1M token month with 70/30 input/output split?

Appreciate it,
Emily

---
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@datafirst.ai>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@datafirst.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: split of system/tool tokens and rounding policy

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise summary you can circulate with finance and engineering; I included our billing rules and a short example at the end. I also looped in our billing and product leads for any edge cases.

1) High-level token buckets
- Input tokens: everything that arrives to the model as part of the prompt for that API call. That includes user messages, the active system message(s) that are sent with the request, and any assistant messages included in the prompt context.
- Output tokens: all tokens the model generates in response (streamed or final).
- Tool tokens: tokens produced by a tool invocation (for example, a reranker response or a scraped text blob returned by a tool). We surface these on invoices as a separate "tool_output" line so customers can clearly see what came from model generation vs tool returns.

2) Attribution for system messages
- System messages are counted as part of the request's input tokens. If you pin a long system prompt and reuse it across many calls via the SDK, each API call that includes it will count those system tokens in its input total. We do not pro-rate system tokens across multiple calls automatically.

3) Tool-call behavior
- If a request triggers a tool:
  * tokens consumed to call the tool (tool input) are counted as input on the initiating request.
  * tokens returned by the tool are invoiced as "tool_output" (separate from model generated output).
  * If the model then consumes the tool output as part of a follow-up prompt, those tokens will again appear as input on the follow-up request (so you can see the chain of custody).
  This separation prevents double-charging for generated content while giving transparency into where tokens originate.

4) Rounding and aggregation
- Per-request: we count exact token integers for each request and then apply a ceiling to the token counts at the request level (i.e., fractional tokens from internal counting are rounded up to the next whole token for that request).
- Invoice aggregation: after request-level token integers are summed for the billing period, we apply discounts and tiering to the aggregated totals. We do NOT apply additional coarse bucketing (e.g., rounding to nearest 10) during invoice aggregation — all price math uses the sum of integer token counts.
- Streaming: tokens emitted during a streaming response are billed as output tokens at the time they are flushed; if a stream is aborted mid-response the partial output tokens are billed (after the per-request ceiling).

5) Example (1,000,000 tokens month, 70/30 input/output split)
- Input tokens (billed): 700,000 (sum of request-level integer counts after per-request ceiling)
- Output tokens (billed): 300,000
- Tool_output (billed separately): depends on your usage; for the sample above assume 50,000 tool tokens -> billed separately as tool_output line item

I'll attach the latest hosted ratecard and a sample invoice calc (PDF + MAP). If you want, we can produce a mock invoice with your actual call distributions.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Emily — hi, Monica from Billing here. A couple of clarifications on how discounts and tiering are applied (so finance can model net spend accurately):

- Volume tiers are evaluated on aggregated monthly token usage across the account (input + output + tool_output separate line items) — not per-route.
- Committed discounts are applied to the committed baseline first. Any usage above commitment is billed at list price and then volume tiering/credits are applied per the contract language (we can lay this out in the MAP).
- Proration: if you sign mid-month, we prorate the commitment for that partial month.
- Invoicing detail: invoices break out input, output, and tool_output lines with raw token counts, unit price, and extended line price so you can map back to engineering telemetry.

I'll attach the ratecard PDF with the exact unit prices and the MAP that Ben referenced. Happy to run a one-off sample invoice using your sample data once Emily shares the call distribution CSV.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Emily — product note from Markus: a couple of implementation specifics that affect counts and are worth flagging to your engineers:

- KV-cache / prefix reuse: if you maintain a client-side cache and send cached snippets as part of the prompt, those tokens are counted as input every time they are sent. If instead you use Redwood's prefix-caching feature we can avoid re-sending the same bytes and they won't be billed per-request.
- Deduplication: when a tool returns content and the model immediately echoes the same content, our pipeline attempts to detect and avoid double-counting generated tokens in the tool_output vs model output. The detection is conservative (we prefer under-counting the second time) so you may still see both items on the invoice if your flow intentionally re-injects the tool result as raw text.

Happy to jump on a short call with your engineers if you'd like to walk through an example trace.

-Markus
